title: How increases in housing costs impact households
meta_description: Housing costs likely to be more expensive to renew, both fixed rate mortgages and renting

breadcrumb.text: How increases in housing costs impact households

lede: Mortgage interest rates started to increase during 2022, this is likely to make borrowing more expensive for those with fixed rates deals coming to an end in 2023. Those with variable rate mortgages and private renters are also facing higher housing costs.

body.text: 9 January 2023
More than 1.4 million households in the UK are facing the prospect of interest rate rises when they renew their fixed rate mortgages in 2023.

The majority of fixed rate mortgages in the UK (57%) coming up for renewal in 2023 were fixed at interest rates below 2%. Those deals that are due to mature through the course of 2024 will be from two-year fixed rate deals made in 2022 and five-year fixed rate deals made in 2019, when mortgage rates were generally higher than 2%.

body.text: BoE data also show that most mortgages are agreed at a fixed interest rate, where the interest rates stay the same for the duration of the mortgage deal, with 86% of outstanding UK mortgages being repaid at fixed interest rates in Quarter 3 (July to Sept) 2022. This is up from 51% in Quarter 1 (Jan to Mar) 2016.

body.h3: The additional costs facing those refixing their mortgages
body.text: The additional costs facing those refixing their mortgages

body.h3: The additional costs facing those refixing their mortgages
body.text: The effective interest rate on outstanding mortgages with a fixed rate was 2.08% in November 2022, according to the BoE. This contrasts with an average interest rate of 4.41% on variable rate mortgages and [quoted household interest rates](https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/statistics/visual-summaries/quoted-household-interest-rates) on new fixed rate mortgages around 6%.

body.h3: The additional costs facing those refixing their mortgages
body.text: When mortgage rates increase, the cost of repayment increases. Looking at different indicative amounts left to repay on mortgages - from £100,000 to £500,000 - we can see the monthly costs that households may face in different scenarios with varying interest rates on the mortgage.

body.h3: The additional costs facing those refixing their mortgages
body.text: Should the interest rate on a £100,000 mortgage increase from 2% to 6%, assuming a 25-year capital and repayment mortgage, then the monthly mortgage repayment on the same mortgage would increase by £220 (from £424 to £644). However, assuming the same increase on a £300,000 mortgage, monthly repayments would rise by £661 (from £1,272 to £1,933).

body.h3: The additional costs facing those refixing their mortgages
body.text: The [BoE's Financial Stability Report - December 2022](https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/financial-stability-report/2022/december-2022) suggests that mortgagors on fixed rates set to expire by the end of 2023 are facing monthly repayment increases of around £250 upon refinancing to a new fixed rate.

body.h3: Private renters are paying more in housing costs
body.text: Private renters are also facing an increase to their housing costs, with rental price growth at its highest rate in the UK since records began in 2016.

body.h3: Private renters are paying more in housing costs
body.text: Around a quarter (26%) of all renters surveyed between 7 and 18 December 2022, reported their rent payments had gone up in the last six months, according to data from the [Opinions and Lifestyle Survey (OPN)](https://www.ons.gov.uk/releases/publicopinionsandsocialtrendsgreatbritain7to18december2022).

body.h3: Private renters are paying more in housing costs
body.text: Private rental prices paid by tenants in the UK rose by 4% in the 12 months to November 2022, up from 3.8% in the 12 months to October 2022, according to data from the [Index of Private Housing Rental Prices](https://www.ons.gov.uk/economy/inflationandpriceindices/bulletins/indexofprivatehousingrentalprices/November2022).

body.h2: Renters spend almost a quarter of their median weekly expenditure on rent
body.text: Renters spend almost a quarter of their median weekly expenditure on rent

body.h2: Renters spend almost a quarter of their median weekly expenditure on rent
body.text: Increases in housing costs can be expected to affect households differently, depending on whether they rent or own their own home. In the year to March 2021, renters in the UK spent a total of £106.50 per week on rent once housing benefit, rebates and other allowances received were accounted for.

body.h2: Renters spend almost a quarter of their median weekly expenditure on rent
body.text: This is equivalent to 24% of their median weekly expenditure. Meanwhile, mortgage holders spent a total of £140.80 per week on mortgage repayments, equal to 16% of their median weekly expenditure.

body.h2: Renters spend almost a quarter of their median weekly expenditure on rent
body.text: While rising housing costs will affect households across the income distribution, they are more likely to disproportionately affect those who already spend a greater proportion of their household spending on housing costs.

body.h2: Renters spend almost a quarter of their median weekly expenditure on rent
body.text: Weekly expenditure on housing is highest for renters in the ninth income decile at £196.20 per week, while mortgage holders in this decile paid £161.50 per week.

body.h2: Renters spend almost a quarter of their median weekly expenditure on rent
body.text: When we look at this as a proportion of expenditure, renters in the second income decile spend on average the greatest proportion (30%) of their expenditure on rent. While for mortgage holders, those in the second income decile, spend a comparably smaller proportion of their total expenditure on mortgage repayments (18%).

body.h2: Renters spend almost a quarter of their median weekly expenditure on rent
body.text: We avoid using the first (lowest 10%) and tenth (highest 10%) income deciles as these can include, for example, households with low income but high wealth, which distorts the picture. Using the second and ninth decile provides a reliable picture of the financial experience of households at the lower and higher end of the income distribution.

body.h2: Around 4 in 10 of those with a mortgage are worried about changes in interest rates on their mortgage
body.text: While the method of securing accommodation differs, in these times of increased cost, both rent and mortgage payers have found them increasingly difficult to service, according to people asked in [our latest OPN survey](https://www.ons.gov.uk/releases/publicopinionsandsocialtrendsgreatbritain7to18december2022).

body.h2: Around 4 in 10 of those with a mortgage are worried about changes in interest rates on their mortgage
body.text: There has been a slight increase in the percentage of people surveyed who, when asked how easy or difficult it was to afford their rent or mortgage payments, said they found it somewhat difficult or very difficult, from 27% in the period 14 to 25 September 2022 to 31% in the period from 7 to 18 December 2022.

body.h2: Around 4 in 10 of those with a mortgage are worried about changes in interest rates on their mortgage
body.text: Additionally, around 4 in 10 (45%) adults with mortgages reported being very or somewhat worried about the changes in mortgage interest rates during the period 7 to 18 December 2022.

body.text: Impact of coronavirus (COVID-19)

body.h2: Around 4 in 10 of those with a mortgage are worried about changes in interest rates on their mortgage
body.text: Restrictions put in place to slow the spread of coronavirus (COVID-19) impacted both spending trends (with certain activities and retail venues closed to the public for periods of lockdown) and data collection, with interviews carried out by telephone rather than face-to-face.

body.h2: Around 4 in 10 of those with a mortgage are worried about changes in interest rates on their mortgage
body.text: In addition, respondents were asked to provide copies of receipts (electronic or paper) for the two-week diary period; and interviewers recorded non-receipt based expenditure via additional regular telephone calls during the two-week diary period.

body.h2: Around 4 in 10 of those with a mortgage are worried about changes in interest rates on their mortgage
body.text: This release discusses income decile groups, or 10ths of households. Households for all of the UK, have been ranked in ascending order of household unequalised gross income (original income combined with cash benefits) then divided into quintile groups to examine expenditure patterns across income groups.

body.h2: Around 4 in 10 of those with a mortgage are worried about changes in interest rates on their mortgage
body.text: Income deciles divide the household income distribution into 10 equal parts. Households with the smallest income lie in the first decile and those with the largest income lie in the top decile.

body.text: Glossary

body.h2: Around 4 in 10 of those with a mortgage are worried about changes in interest rates on their mortgage
body.text: Fixed rate mortgage: The interest rate on the outstanding loan amount remains fixed for a certain period of time. Typically, between two and five years.

body.h2: Around 4 in 10 of those with a mortgage are worried about changes in interest rates on their mortgage
body.text: Variable rate mortgage: The interest rate on the outstanding loan amount varies over the course of the repayment period because of changes in market conditions.

body.h2: Around 4 in 10 of those with a mortgage are worried about changes in interest rates on their mortgage
body.text: Effective interest rate: The weighted average of all the interest rates across each type of deposit or loan account held by all the clients within an economic sector.

body.h2: Around 4 in 10 of those with a mortgage are worried about changes in interest rates on their mortgage
body.text: Quoted household interest rate: The weighted averages for a range of lending and deposit products offered to households.

body.h2: Around 4 in 10 of those with a mortgage are worried about changes in interest rates on their mortgage
body.text: Capital and repayment mortgage: Mortgage is repaid through monthly repayments for an agreed period of time (known as the "term") until the loan amount is repaid. The term is usually 25 years.

body.h2: Around 4 in 10 of those with a mortgage are worried about changes in interest rates on their mortgage
body.text: Bank Rate: Sometimes called the "Bank of England base rate", the Bank Rate determines the interest rate that the Bank of England pays to Commercial Banks who hold money with them. This, in turn, influences the interest rates those banks charge people to borrow money.

body.h2: Around 4 in 10 of those with a mortgage are worried about changes in interest rates on their mortgage
body.text: Renters: Renters are householders who rent from local authorities and private landlords, furnished or unfurnished. Householders who are purchasing through rental purchase are also included in this category, in line with family spending (see our [Family spending in the UK: April 2020 to March 2021 bulletin).](https://www.ons.gov.uk/peoplepopulationandcommunity/personalandhouseholdfinances/expenditure/bulletins/familyspendingintheuk/april2020tomarch2021)

body.h2: Around 4 in 10 of those with a mortgage are worried about changes in interest rates on their mortgage
body.text: Mortgage holders: Mortgage households are households who own their property via a mortgage, in line with family spending.
